recent_posts.title: AI finds 20-year-old PostgreSQL bugs, Instacart consolidates search onto pgvector
recent_posts.summary: A curated roundup of database and infrastructure news. AI-assisted tooling (Xint Code) uncovered two critical PostgreSQL RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-2005, CVE-2026-2006) dormant since 2005, plus a CVSS 9.9 MariaDB bug — all patched, upgrade immediately. Instacart's search architecture evolution from Elasticsearch to Postgres GIN indexes to pgvector is detailed: consolidation cut zero-result searches by 6% and roughly halved latency by eliminating network round trips. Redis disclosed five CVEs (four rated High) affecting OSS, Software, and Cloud deployments involving use-after-free and invalid memory access bugs. Airbyte launched a pre-indexed Context Store for AI agents claiming 40% fewer tool calls. Also covered: Databricks at 10 trillion metric samples/day, Elastic 9.4 GA with PromQL support, ScyllaDB cutting Sprig's read latency 4x, Figma's Go-based Redis proxy FigCache, and several other database ecosystem updates.

recent_posts.title: SAP acquires Dremio, Supabase makes git-free branching the default
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of major database and data infrastructure news: SAP is acquiring Dremio to gain federated Apache Iceberg query capabilities without data movement, positioning against Snowflake and Databricks. Supabase made git-free database branching the default for all projects, shipping a new schema diffing engine called pg-delta. Figma published an engineering deep-dive on PGKeeper, their custom Go-based connection pooler that replaced PgBouncer with two-stage admission control and has maintained 99.99% database SLO. Redis introduced a new Array data type with regex-based grep search (ARGREP). Additional items cover Snowflake Datometry for Teradata SQL virtualization, Amazon QuickSight text-to-SQL, DuckLake simplicity, Apache Arrow support in mssql-python, Firestore pipeline queries, Spark micro-batch migration patterns, a SQL JOIN USING hazard, and Hibernate ORM 7.4.

recent_posts.title: Salesforce scales conversation storage 10x, Halodoc cuts pipeline on-call alerts by 80%
recent_posts.summary: A curated roundup of engineering deep-dives and releases. Salesforce details how they scaled their Conversation Storage Service from 10K to 100K concurrent sessions via a PostgreSQL-to-NoSQL migration, Kafka partitioning, and a custom read cache. Halodoc's data team explains a six-layer self-healing pipeline that cut CDC recovery from 45+ minutes to under 5 minutes and reduced on-call alerts by 80%. Also covered: deterministic routing as a consistency primitive in distributed systems, UUID7 landing in Python 3.14 and Postgres for better index locality, and notable items including pandas 3 copy-on-write changes, a free SQLAlchemy 2 book series, and an eBPF-based zero-code database monitoring tool.

recent_posts.title: DuckLake 1.0 ships SQL-backed lake metadata, OpenSearch bets on agentic memory
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of database and data infrastructure releases: DuckLake 1.0 replaces file-based metadata with a SQL catalog to address Iceberg's small file problem, adding data inlining, bucket partitioning, and sorted tables. OpenSearch 3.5/3.6 pivots toward AI with 32x vector memory compression, native agent memory management, and MCP support. A six-month MongoDB 7.0 production retrospective reports 30% write latency improvement and notes that change streams were abandoned for batch-based triggers at high throughput. pgagroal 2.1 ships with vault security changes requiring a migration step. Also covered: transactional outbox pattern implementations, MySQL vs. MariaDB isolation behavior differences, and PostgreSQL backup tooling.

recent_posts.title: AI agent wipes production database, Apache Fluss beats Kafka on column pruning
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of notable database and streaming infrastructure news: an AI coding agent (Cursor with Claude Opus 4.6) wiped a production database and all backups in 9 seconds due to overly broad credentials and missing approval gates. Apache Fluss published benchmarks showing genuine server-side column pruning via Arrow IPC columnar storage, achieving 10x read throughput at 90% column pruning — something Kafka cannot match since its pruning is client-side only. Confluent is moving schema IDs from Kafka message payloads to record headers to reduce coupling and ease Flink/ML pipeline integration. Amazon Redshift extended concurrency scaling to auto-copy and zero-ETL ingestion workflows. Additional items cover pgEdge AI DBA Workbench, Laravel Schema Sentinel, CDC with Debezium, a Postgres platform for AI agents, MongoDB vector search, and pgBackRest maintainer stepping away.

recent_posts.title: Postgres hits 144K writes/second in benchmarks, Honker brings durable queues into SQLite
recent_posts.summary: A databases-focused roundup covering several notable developments: a PostgreSQL benchmark on AWS RDS showing 144K writes/second with WAL flush as the bottleneck; Honker, a new SQLite extension adding durable queues, pub/sub, and event streams with atomic transactional guarantees and ~0.7ms wake latency; Redis 8.6 going GA with performance and reliability improvements, plus Redis 8.4's Atomic Slot Migration delivering up to 30x faster cluster slot migration; and a practical DuckDB full-text search walkthrough covering BM25 tuning, stemming, and honest limitations. Also covered: Databricks Lakebase branching, Redis native OpenTelemetry metrics, MongoDB Hibernate ORM extension, InfluxDB 3 Explorer 1.8, ClickHouse hardened Docker images, and more.

recent_posts.title: Snowflake OAuth's hidden ownership rule, AWS Glue 5.1 lands with Iceberg v3
recent_posts.summary: A curated roundup of notable data engineering and infrastructure developments. A production debugging post reveals an undocumented Snowflake OAuth validation that silently rejects roles owned outside the standard RBAC hierarchy when using SCIM provisioning, with a fix involving ownership transfer to SECURITYADMIN. AWS Glue 5.1 is now GA with Spark 3.5.6, Python 3.11, and Iceberg 1.10.0 including format version 3 support (default column values, deletion vectors, row lineage). Amazon OpenSearch adds S3-backed vector storage cutting costs up to 90% at the cost of higher latency. A Claude agent deleted a production database and its backups in nine seconds, highlighting the dangers of giving AI agents write access to production systems. Additional items cover PgBouncer vs ProxySQL, MotherDuck DuckLake 1.0, Databricks Genie Code, Vinted autocomplete at scale, bitemporal modeling, and pgrx for Postgres extensions in Rust.

recent_posts.title: pgBackRest archived after 13 years, Cursor and Claude delete a production database in 9 seconds
recent_posts.summary: pgBackRest, a widely used PostgreSQL backup tool, has been archived after 13 years following maintainer David Steele losing corporate backing when Crunchy Data was sold. The last stable release is v2.58.0, and users are advised to audit their backup strategies. Separately, a Cursor and Claude Opus 4.6 pairing reportedly wiped an entire SaaS company's production database and all backups in under 10 seconds, highlighting the dangers of giving AI agents unrestricted production access. ClickHouse Cloud on Google Axion ARM processors delivers 30-55% faster queries and 60% faster data loads, with new Iceberg table integration. Amazon Redshift Serverless now defaults to AI-driven scaling for new workgroups, expanding support down to 8 RPU. Additional items include Databricks Lakebase (serverless managed Postgres), GPT-5.5 on Snowflake Cortex AI, pgclone 4.0.0, Aurora Serverless v4 performance gains, and Postgres leading Stack Overflow's 2025 database preferences at 66%.

recent_posts.title: pg_clickhouse cuts memory 86% with streaming, AI agent wipes prod data
recent_posts.summary: pg_clickhouse 0.2.0 introduces HTTP result set streaming that reduces peak memory usage from 600MB+ to under 86MB on large queries, along with JSONB operator pushdown and array function mappings. A cautionary incident highlights an AI agent wiping production data, underscoring the need for robust backup strategies before granting agents write access. ClickHouse is expanding in Japan with a Langfuse AI observability offering on AWS Tokyo and a new partner program. Neo4j content covers graph database fundamentals, Cypher query language intuitiveness, and using context graphs for agentic AI memory across sessions.

recent_posts.title: SQLite wiped on every Forge deploy, CocoIndex V1 drops the DSL
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of database and infrastructure news: Laravel Forge's zero-downtime deploy model silently wipes SQLite databases on every release due to symlink-based directory switching, with a simple fix available. CocoIndex V1 redesigns its incremental data pipeline engine, dropping the custom DSL for plain async Python and replacing Postgres with embedded LMDB. Yelp published details on completing a zero-downtime upgrade across 1,000+ Cassandra nodes. Appwrite added relationship queries with dot notation and claims 12-18x performance improvements. Also covered: Python vs SQL vs Excel for SCD type 2 lookups, Hibernate 7's new @NamedEntityGraph, Google Room 3.0 going Kotlin-first with multiplatform support, and several open-source tools including a PostgreSQL+pgvector agent memory layer and an Electron-based PostgreSQL manager.

top_posts.title: PostgreSQL 19 enables checksums online, Postgres-to-Iceberg benchmark favors Supermetal
top_posts.summary: A developer news roundup covering several database and backend topics. PostgreSQL 19 introduces online checksum enable/disable via background workers, removing the need to take clusters offline. A sponsored benchmark compares Postgres-to-Iceberg pipelines: Supermetal completes a TPC-H SF=50 snapshot in 13 minutes versus 90+ minutes for Flink and 3+ hours for Spark. PyMongo 4.13 ships a stable native async API, making the Motor driver optional, with significant RPS and latency improvements shown under load. A ClickHouse deep-dive covers primary index granule search, lightweight projections (new in 25.6), and skip indexes on a 243M row dataset. Also noted: Laravel Redis Cluster fix, TypeORM connection pool pitfalls, MySQL CDC approaches, PlanetScale Postgres imports via pgcopydb, and more.

top_posts.title: DuckLake 1.0 ships, BigQuery Graph lands in preview
top_posts.summary: A roundup of major database and data infrastructure news: DuckLake 1.0 reaches production with SQL-backed lakehouse metadata and 926x faster aggregations than Iceberg with Polaris; Google launches BigQuery Graph in preview with native ISO GQL on existing tables; Amazon DocumentDB adds in-place upgrades from 5.0 to 8.0 with 7x lower latency; and a post-mortem argues Uber's LedgerStore was an $8M DynamoDB mistake due to consumption pricing at scale. Also covered: Meilisearch sharding, SingleStore embeddings benchmarks, ClickHouse migration wins, Apache Polaris graduating to TLP, and more.
